circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, the Yas Marina Circuit is a 5. 281 km track designed by Hermann Tilke that has served as the Formula One season finale since 2009. The circuit represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One venue, following Bahrain and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit winds around a lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb and hosts the annual Australian Grand Prix as its premier motorsport event. The FIA Grade 1 facility also accommodates the Supercars Championship and various supporting races throughout the season.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit has hosted the Austrian Grand Prix across two separate periods in its history. Originally established as the Österreichring in 1970, it held the race annually until 1987, then after being redesigned and shortened, it returned as a grand prix venue from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is an urban racing venue situated in Azerbaijan's capital, featuring a 6. 003 km lap that ranks as the fourth-longest track in Formula One competition. The circuit first hosted a grand prix in 2016 as the European Grand Prix, before becoming the permanent home of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted the first Middle Eastern Formula One Grand Prix and continues to hold the annual race alongside hosting drag racing, GP2 Series events, and 24-hour endurance competitions. The track, which features multiple configurations and holds a FIA Grade 1 license, previously hosted the Desert 400 featuring Australian V8 Supercars from 2006 until their withdrawal from the schedule in 2011.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for all racing disciplines. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 license and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Located in the Belgian Ardennes region near the town of Spa, this 7-kilometer circuit has been a fixture of Formula One racing since 1950, when it featured on the championship's inaugural season. The venue has continuously hosted the Belgian Grand Prix annually since 1985, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km temporary street circuit that hosts the FIA Formula One Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond its primary role in Formula One racing, the venue has served as a home for various international motorsport series, including world sportscar, open-wheel, and stock car competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading district, this Chinese motorsport venue hosted the Chinese Grand Prix intermittently, with races from 2004 to 2019 and resuming from 2024. The circuit has expanded its racing calendar to include electric motorsport events alongside its traditional Formula One championship rounds.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near Silverstone in Northamptonshire, England, this racing facility has been the traditional venue for the British Grand Prix since 1948 and notably hosted the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. After alternating with Aintree and Brands Hatch for several decades, the circuit became the permanent home of the British Grand Prix from 1987 onwards, while also hosting the MotoGP British round.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Mogyoród, is a 4. 381 km circuit that hosted Formula One's inaugural Grand Prix behind the Iron Curtain in 1986. Built remarkably swiftly in just eight months starting from October 1985, the track was constructed on a greenfield site near a major highway after plans for a street circuit in Budapest's central park were abandoned.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Situated near Milan in northern Italy, the Autodromo Nazionale di Monza spans 5. 793 km and ranks among Europe's oldest purpose-built racing venues, having opened in 1922. The circuit has continuously hosted the Italian Grand Prix since 1949, apart from a 1980 closure for renovation, making it one of Formula One's most enduring venues and earning its reputation as "the Temple of Speed" for its fast, flowing layout.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km motorsport facility situated in Mie Prefecture, Japan and run by Honda Mobilityland. The track hosts major international racing series, most notably Formula One and Japanese Super Formula championships, with a spectator capacity of 155,000.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, alongside the famous Las Vegas Boulevard. The track weaves past iconic casino resorts and entertainment venues, including Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, as well as the MSG Sphere.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: The Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit in Mexico City named after two Mexican racing brothers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, both of whom died in racing accidents during the 1960s. The venue returned to Formula One's calendar in 2015 after a 23-year absence, hosting the Mexican Grand Prix on a revised layout, with the event rebranded as the Mexico City Grand Prix from 2021 onwards.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary road course constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 turns designed specifically for Formula One racing. Since joining the F1 calendar in 2022, the circuit has become the home of the Miami Grand Prix, with qualifying speeds averaging approximately 139 mph around its purpose-built configuration.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The 3. 337 km street circuit winds through the Monte Carlo district of the Principality of Monaco, following city streets around the harbour area and extending into La Condamine. The track is predominantly situated within Monte Carlo, which is why it carries that name both formally and colloquially.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track known for its dramatic elevation changes and steeply banked corners that create an exhilarating racing experience. The venue hosted the Dutch Grand Prix from 2021 until 2026, when its Formula One partnership concluded, having earned the affectionate nickname "The Roller coaster in the Dunes" for its unique topography among fans.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit sits near Lusail city, north of Doha, and spans 5. 419 kilometers with a 1. 068-kilometer main straight.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian racing venue in São Paulo that opened in 1940 and was later renamed after Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who tragically died in a 1977 aviation accident. The counterclockwise track is notable for hosting major motorsport events and features an associated kart facility dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue positioned along Jeddah's waterfront beside the Red Sea in Saudi Arabia. Since its debut in 2021, the track has hosted the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix, and recently began accommodating Formula E racing from 2025 onward.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit is a street-based racing layout positioned around Singapore's Marina Bay, incorporating the Downtown Core and Kallang urban zones.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya near Barcelona spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of high-speed straights and diverse corner types, making it a versatile test for drivers and teams. Located in Montmeló with an FIA Grade 1 license, the venue can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the track hosts major international motorsport events including MotoGP, the World Endurance Championship, and NASCAR competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British motorsport competitor currently racing for Williams in Formula One, competing under the Thai flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has claimed two world championships during his 23-season career while accumulating 32 race victories. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance motorsport, including two Le Mans victories and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to have won both a Formula One drivers' title and a world endurance championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli made his Formula One debut in 2025 and currently races for Mercedes, where he has already secured nine Grand Prix victories.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Haas, where he competes at the highest level of motorsport.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races in Formula One representing the Audi team. Bortoleto has established himself as a competitor in the sport's top tier motorseries.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing considerable experience from his 13 seasons in the sport. He achieved two World Championship runner-up finishes while with Mercedes in 2019 and 2020, accumulating 10 Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto, an Argentine racing driver, currently races for Alpine in Formula One.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The racing driver previously achieved a significant victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar represents France in Formula One, competing for Red Bull Racing. The driver holds both French and Algerian nationality.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari who shares the record for most world championship titles with seven victories. The accomplished competitor holds multiple circuit records, including the most race wins, pole positions, and podium appearances in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One. Beyond single-seater competition, he achieved endurance racing success by winning the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson, a New Zealand-born racing driver, currently races for Racing Bulls in the Formula One championship.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver, races for Ferrari in Formula One and has claimed nine Grand Prix victories throughout his career. He finished second in the 2022 world championship standings while competing for the Scuderia.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen, a Danish driver competing since 2014, has spent his Formula One career across two separate periods, most recently through 2024. Currently, he focuses on endurance racing as a BMW factory driver for WRT in the World Endurance Championship, while also participating part-time in NASCAR's top series with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris is a British Formula One driver currently competing for McLaren, where he claimed the 2025 World Drivers' Championship. The driver has accumulated 13 Grand Prix victories throughout his eight seasons in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. Previously competing for Alpine, he achieved a Grand Prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio "Checo" Pérez represents Mexico in Formula One racing with Cadillac. The experienced competitor finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull and has accumulated six race victories throughout his lengthy 15-season career in the sport.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver, races for McLaren in Formula One and has secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his four-season career in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known by the nickname "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight race victories during his career in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell competes for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has secured eight Grand Prix victories throughout his career spanning eight seasons.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: American driver Logan Sargeant raced in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to other racing series. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, having previously campaigned in IMSA's LMP2 class.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin, where he continues to compete at the highest level of motorsport.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese motorsport competitor, holds reserve positions with both Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in Formula One. After five seasons as a full-time driver from 2021 through 2025, he transitioned to a backup role beginning in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch-Belgian driver Max Verstappen races for Red Bull Racing and has secured four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024. With 73 Grand Prix victories accumulated over his 12-season career, he stands among Formula One's most successful drivers.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu holds the distinction of being China's sole Formula One competitor, having raced in the series from 2022 through 2024, and currently functions as a reserve driver for Cadillac.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has competed as Alpine F1 since 2021, adopting the name to represent Renault's sports car division while functioning as the manufacturer's official entry. Previously operating under the Renault banner since the automotive giant's return to the sport, Alpine maintained this works status until Renault's withdrawal at the conclusion of the 2025 season.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin is a British automotive manufacturer with a long history in Formula One racing, competing under various team structures throughout its involvement in the sport. The current iteration operates as AMR GP Limited and races under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari HP represents the racing arm of the Italian luxury car manufacturer Ferrari in Formula One competition. As motorsport's longest-tenured and most accomplished outfit, the team has maintained an unbroken presence in the World Championship since its inception in 1950, earning the popular moniker "the Prancing Horse" after their distinctive emblem.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: An American-licensed Formula One outfit founded by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas, the squad entered the championship in 2016 with relatively modest resources compared to established rivals. Under current team principal Ayao Komatsu, who assumed leadership after Guenther Steiner's departure in early 2024, the team has established itself as a consistent midfield competitor in the sport.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss engineering outfit founded in 1970, the team initially built sports cars before transitioning to Formula One in 1993 as an independent constructor, achieving notable success in endurance racing including victory at Le Mans in 1989. After over three decades competing in F1 through various ownership changes, the team concluded its participation in 2025 as the sport's fourth-longest-serving constructor, subsequently becoming the foundation for Audi's entry into the championship when acquired in 2024.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered at its technology facility in Woking that competes under sponsorship arrangements. The team operates as part of the broader McLaren Group structure, with ownership held by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has competed in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier, with the current iteration based in Brackley and racing under a German licence. The team, now known as Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One Team, became jointly owned by Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff from January 2022. Mercedes-affiliated squads are traditionally nicknamed the "Silver Arrows" in racing circles.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that commenced competition in 2024 as part of Red Bull's two-team operation. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility near Milton Keynes, the squad functions as a sister team to Red Bull Racing under Austrian ownership.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that began competing in 2024 as one of two teams owned by Red Bull GmbH, alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with an additional facility near Milton Keynes, the squad operates as Red Bull's second constructor in the championship.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing represents one of two Formula One operations controlled by Red Bull GmbH and operates under an Austrian license from its English headquarters. Established in 2005, the team was steered by Christian Horner for two decades before Laurent Mekies assumed leadership in 2025.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Atlassian Williams F1 Team is a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, rising from the ashes of Williams's previous failed racing venture. Headquartered at a sprawling facility in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team has competed continuously in the sport for nearly five decades.
